title: Muscle soak bath salts
subtitle: Epsom salts with eucalyptus and black pepper for a hot bath
excerpt: Muscle soak bath salts are a blend of Epsom salts, sea salt, and bicarbonate of soda, fragranced with eucalyptus and black pepper essential oils. A large handful added to a hot bath dissolves quickly; the heat and buoyancy do the work for tired muscles. Makes 500 g in a jar; keeps twelve months sealed in a dry cupboard.
sourceNotes: Epsom salts (magnesium sulphate) bath use: widely documented; magnesium transdermal absorption from bath water remains debated in the literature (published studies by Zechner et al. 2011). The claim made here is that the hot bath and buoyancy relax muscles, which is uncontroversial, not a specific magnesium absorption claim. Black pepper essential oil in a bath soak: The Complete Book of Essential Oils and Aromatherapy by Valerie Wormwood (1991). Eucalyptus for inhalation during a bath: Australian Tea Tree Industry Association technical notes.

recipe.yieldDescription: 500 g bath salts (~10 baths of 50 g each)
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple and store in a large airtight jar. Keep a dry scoop inside the jar.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix in a large batch. The salts absorb the essential oils quickly; the blend is ready to use immediately.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Twelve months in a sealed dry container. Salts clump when exposed to humidity, keep the lid on and the jar away from the bath during use.

glossaryTerms.definition: Magnesium sulphate crystals, widely used in bath preparations. The salts dissolve readily in warm water and give the bath water a slightly silky texture.

content.text: Combine the Epsom salts, sea salt, and bicarbonate of soda in a large bowl and mix. Add the essential oils drop by drop and stir thoroughly to distribute them evenly through the salts, clumps of undiluted essential oil on the skin sting. Pour into a sealed jar.

Add 50 to 100 g to a hot bath as the water is running, so the salts dissolve fully before getting in. Soak for 15 to 20 minutes. Pat dry after the bath rather than rubbing, which retains more of the oil from the bath water on the skin.
Twelve months in a sealed jar. Keep the lid on between uses, salts absorb humidity and clump if left exposed. Use a dry scoop to avoid introducing moisture.
